name: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Ḥarīsh al-Hamdānī, called Abū Misḥal
summary: Bedouin grammarian and pupil of al-Kisāʾī, learned in the Qurʾān and its iʿrāb, who came to Baghdad to the vizier al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl.
bio: Abū Misḥal, whose kunya was Abū Muḥammad, was a Bedouin learned in the Qurʾān and the ways of its iʿrāb, who knew the ʿarabiyya well and learned from al-Kisāʾī. He came to Baghdad to present himself to al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the third generation of the grammarians of Kufa.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 221–222
